Archaic

/ahr-KAY-ik/ — rhymes with mosaic · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Archaic means belonging to an earlier period of time and no longer in current use.

Much of his vocabulary felt archaic, so tied to his own century that Priya sometimes had to guess at his meaning.

Worked Example

In her grandmother's attic, Maya found archaic letters written in a spidery hand, words she'd never seen before because the language itself had changed so much.

Archaic means something is not just old, but specifically old and no longer in use. It's more precise than "ancient" (which emphasizes age but not disuse) or "old" (which says nothing about whether the thing is still used). These letters belong to a vanished era of language — that's exactly what archaic captures.

How Archaic Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

ancient

ancient: extremely old — often thousands of years old

obsolete

obsolete: simply discarded — replaced by something newer

outdated

outdated: just behind the times, not from a vanished era

Antonyms

modern

modern: new and belonging to the present day

current

current: still in active, everyday use right now

How Strong Is It? — outdated → old-fashioned → archaic

outdated vs. archaic

outdated vs. archaic: An outdated bus schedule is much weaker than archaic — it is only a little behind the times, and one quick reprint makes it useful again.

old-fashioned vs. archaic

old-fashioned vs. archaic: An old-fashioned handwritten thank-you note is weaker than archaic — it feels quaint and charming, but people still happily write and receive them today.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of archaic.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — archa-

Root — archa-: ancient, old (from Greek arkhaios 'ancient, old-fashioned,' itself built on arkhē, 'beginning, origin')

Suffix — -ic

Suffix — -ic: characteristic of, having the quality of

Put it together

Put it together: Archa- (ancient, old — Greek arkhaios, built on arkhē, 'beginning') + -ic (characteristic of) builds the meaning literally: having the character of ancient times — so old-fashioned it seems to belong to an earlier era. Note the spelling: the Greek root keeps its 'ch,' but it is pronounced like 'k' (ar-KAY-ik).

Use the root in a new word: archetype

Use the root in a new word: archetype: The original supermarket layout became the archetype for every supermarket built after it.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Archaic is a scholarly word for things that belong to a vanished past. In everyday speech, say 'old-fashioned' or 'outdated.' Reach for archaic when describing vocabulary, customs, or styles that clearly belong to a historical era.
